title: De-AI Your UI: 5 Fixes for Landing Pages
summary: This reel identifies five common design 'tells' that make a landing page look AI-generated and provides specific fixes to improve professionalism. It covers improvements for headlines, background elements, button hierarchy, social proof, and feature sections.

transcript.text: Your landing page looks AI-made. Five tells, five fixes.
Tell one: 'Supercharge your workflow with AI' - ingredient text. A generated hero sells adjectives because it has no product to name.
Plain text: Say what it does, say for whom. 'Close the month in one afternoon.'
Tell two: The purple blob. A gradient smear behind everything because the page needs energy from somewhere.
Neutral background. The only color goes on the product and one button.
Tell three: 'Get started', 'Learn more'. Same size, side by side. Two equal buttons split the click.
One primary. The second becomes a text link with an arrow.
Tell four: 'Trusted by 10,000+ users'. Five gray logos. A number nobody can check, logos nobody recognizes.
One quote. A name, a role, a result with a unit.
Tell five: Three feature cards, icon in a circle, one line each. Fast, secure, easy. Every generated page has this row.
Replace it with the product. One screenshot, three annotations pointing at real UI.
Five tells, gone. Or type /restyle. UX Engine, the Claude code plugin that kills the AI look. Link in bio.

on_screen_text: TELL 01 - THE HEADLINE: Adjectives are not a product.
TELL 02 - THE BLOB: Color goes on the product.
TELL 04 - THE PROOF: One quote beats ten thousand.
Name - role - result with a unit
TELL 05 - FEATURE CARDS: Show the product.
Show the product - not the adjectives
before_after: A generic, purple-blob-filled AI-generated landing page with vague copy and generic icons is transformed into a clean, product-focused landing page with specific copy, clear hierarchy, and real social proof.
